lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.17 - A Listen and read

details: Listen and read develops reading and listening skills by following a short story about the amusement park and understand key feelings words, past-tense actions, and simple story events.
Look for careful listening and reading, clear tracking of the text, recognition of past tense verbs, and understanding of feeling words.

“Can you remember what I did at the amusement park? What was scary? There were two things! That’s right… the haunted house was scary… and the animals at the petting zoo! Really! I was scared. Do you want to know what happened to Rosa and her friends at the amusement park? Let’s find out!”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.75 - A Read and number.

details: Read and number develops students’ reading comprehension by sequencing the order of what happened at the amusement park.
Look for correct numbering, careful reading, matching each paragraph to the right order, and showing clear understanding of the story sequence.
“Oh, no! The parts of the story are all mixed up! Can you help me put the events in the correct order? I think that you are very good at this!”

Homework Check:
Have Ss open to the previous lesson’s homework. Score completion %. Conduct activity feedback and error correction. Score achievement %. 
Project Gallery:
Check and encourage Ss to complete the project prompts so that they are ready to present by lesson 7,

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.75 - B Read and circle T/F

details: Read and circle T/F checks understanding of the story by identifying correct and incorrect information using simple true-or-false statements.
Look for correct choices, careful reading of each statement, and match ideas to the story accurately.
“I think these sentences are about Rosa, NIck, and Kevin, but I’m not really sure. Let’s read them together to see which sentences are true or false.”

Unscramble tests spelling and vocabulary skills by rearranging jumbled letters to form key story words and associating each word to its corresponding picture.

lessonPlan.topic: Break [10m] - B Choose or write the correct answers

details: Choose or write the correct answers develops reading comprehension by checking how well students understand the story details, past tense actions, and feelings words.
Look for correct picture choices, accurate written words, clear matching of story information, and neat, legible answers.
“I can’t remember what happened to Rosa, Nick, and Kevin at the amusement park. Can you help me choose the correct details so that I can remember?”

lessonPlan.topic: Break [10m] - C Imagine you went to an amusement park. Write and share.

details: Imagine develops students’ creativity by asking them to think about a hypothetical situation. Write and share develops writing skills by using past tense verbs and feeling words to describe simple experiences and share ideas in short, meaningful sentences.
Look for clear past tense verb use, correct feeling words, complete sentences, neat handwriting, and writing that match the task (make sense).
“I need to write a story, but I have no idea what to write. Can you help me by writing about what you and your friend would do at an amusement park?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.18 - D Make your own story.

details: Make your own story gives students the opportunity to practise vocabulary by choosing their own words to go in the gaps to complete a personalised story.
Look for accurate word choices and pronunciation and confident presentation of the completed story.
“Now, it’s your turn to write a story about your day at an amusement park. What words and sentences could you put in the gaps?”
